You are fixing a bug in the Python repository in the current working directory. The bug and the required behavior are described below. Read the relevant source files, make the necessary code edits to the source (do NOT edit the tests), and use the shell to run the tests to confirm your fix. Keep changes minimal.

ISSUE:
Removing a default header of a session
[The docs](http://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/user/advanced/#session-objects) say that you can prevent sending a session header by setting the headers value to None in the method's arguments. You would expect (as [discussed on IRC](https://botbot.me/freenode/python-requests/msg/10788170/)) that this would work for session's default headers, too:

``` python
session = requests.Session()
# Do not send Accept-Encoding
session.headers['Accept-Encoding'] = None
```

What happens is that "None"  gets sent as the value of header.

```
Accept-Encoding: None
```

For the reference, here is a way that works:

``` python
del session.headers['Accept-Encoding']
```



The test suite lives in tests/. You can run it with: python -m pytest -q
When the tests pass, you are done.
[Bash] git stash && python -m pytest -q test_requests.py::RequestsTestCase::test_conflicting_post_params 2>&1 | tail -5; git stash pop

The failing test is a pre-existing failure unrelated to my change (it fails without my edit too). All header-related tests pass. The fix is complete.

The change in `requests/sessions.py` makes `merge_setting` remove any key whose merged value is `None`, so setting a session default header to `None` (e.g. `session.headers['Accept-Encoding'] = None`) now suppresses it instead of sending `None` as the value.
